content: scripts/check-prose.ts's long-paragraph(>6s) rule effectively counts wrapped LINES: every non-empty prose line contributes >=1 fragment, plus one per mid-line sentence split (splitSentences breaks on [.!?:] + whitespace + uppercase). AGENTS.md is grandfathered at exactly its 35-violation ceiling, so any prose added to it must keep each touched paragraph at <=6 wrapped lines and place sentence boundaries at line ends (or split into a new paragraph). Verify the count before committing: bun -e 'import {readFileSync} from "node:fs"; import {lint, countable} from "./scripts/check-prose.ts"; console.log(countable(lint(readFileSync("AGENTS.md","utf8"),25).violations).length)' — must stay <=35. Mirroring an existing passing sentence's wording (e.g. the gen:docs:check bullet) is the safest way to add bullets at zero new violations.

title: Position Warren as coding-agent infrastructure
rationale: The old control-plane and issue-to-PR pitch described architecture and table stakes but did not explain the transition Warren enables. Infrastructure/workload language names both the user trigger and Warren's operational ownership while preserving honest current limits.

content: README top-to-Quickstart must contain none of bwrap/k8s/PAT/machine account/.env. Operator content lives in README #Operators plus docs/credentials.md (single page for the four credential paths). .env.example top block points casual users at 'warren up'. Prose guard (check:prose) runs at threshold 0 for README.md and new untracked docs (quickstart.md, credentials.md): avoid 'executes'/'carries out' (nominalization rule), passive voice, semicolons, and sentences over 25 words.
